Let’s start with Jordan Kim at +1-646-555-0134.

From my current location in San Francisco, calculate the distance to Jordan’s city, then create the lunch reminder using the existing lunch timing context already on my device. After that, search for it and confirm the full saved details: the exact distance result you used, the reminder content, timestamp, any attached latitude/longitude, and the identifier or matching search result showing it was saved correctly.
summary: A toolsandbox ‘device assistant’ run that builds six location-aware reminders — one per contact — each reusing an existing on-device reminder's timestamp as its timing basis. The shape is highly repetitive: T1–T5 each look up a contact, infer the city from the area code, compute the SF-to-city distance, and create a reminder (Jordan/NYC, Emily/Chicago, Sofia/NYC, Monica/SF, Daniel/NYC), while T6 adds the self reminder for Maya Bennett and T7 is the closing summary. The recall load is concentrated on T4–T7, where the agent restates earlier reminders on demand: the first Jordan lunch reminder (T4, T6), the ‘other city’ Emily/Chicago reminder (T5), and the Daniel apartment-cleaning reminder (T6). Behaviorally every probe is COMPLY — the agent recalls IDs, epoch timestamps and coordinates from working memory with no re-fetch — yet only 8/16 subgoals credit, because the grader demands exact machine tokens (full UUIDs and epoch-seconds) and the agent sometimes truncates IDs (e.g. 8eef20b8-...) in its summary tables. A competent run penalized by exact-token grading rigidity, not a memory failure.
